title: JIT-Q: Just-in-time Quantization with Processing-In-Memory for Efficient ML Training
problem: ML training incurs substantial memory bandwidth overhead and compute inefficiency. Applying quantization during training requires efficient mechanisms to reduce precision without sacrificing model accuracy or requiring excessive data movement.
motivation: Reducing memory bandwidth and compute requirements during training enables faster, more energy-efficient training of large-scale ML models.
method: JIT-Q applies quantization dynamically during training while leveraging processing-in-memory (PIM) to execute quantized operations directly within memory hierarchy. By co-locating quantization logic with PIM primitives, the approach minimizes data movement and computes on reduced-precision representations in-place.
key_novelty: Combining just-in-time quantization with processing-in-memory to perform quantized training operations in-situ within memory, eliminating bandwidth-intensive data movement.
contributions: Just-in-time quantization scheme designed for training efficiency
Integration of quantization with processing-in-memory architecture
Demonstration of improved training speedup and energy efficiency
Method for maintaining training convergence and accuracy with reduced precision
limitations: Limitations not discussed from title only
primary_theme: Just-in-time quantization with processing-in-memory for efficient ML training
